 Bucks stop: Bulls bounce back on Giddey's nine dimes
 Written By
 basketball.com.au
 Chicago Bulls’ Josh Giddey moves the ball against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum Center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on October 24, 2026 (AEDT). Photo: Gary Dineen/NBAE via Getty Images. Copyright 2026 NBAE.
 Share now: 
 Nine assists from Giddey, then rookie Wilson came up big as Bulls win their first of the season
 Josh Giddey had six points, a game-high nine assists and four rebounds in 25 minutes 
 Chicago came from 15 down to win 132-125 in Milwaukee after a 43-point opening loss 
 Giddey sat the final 3:56 as Tre Jones closed out a 14-6 finish 
 Josh Giddey's game-high nine assists helped the Chicago Bulls come from 15 down to beat the Milwaukee Bucks 132-125 on Saturday, October 24 (AEDT), with the rest of the Aussies still to play.
 Josh Giddey and the Chicago Bulls opened the day by answering a 43-point opening-night loss with a road win in Milwaukee, the first of seven games involving an Australian on Saturday, October 24 (AEDT). 
 Catch up on every Australian in the league at our Aussies in the NBA hub , and on Friday's results, led by Tyrese Proctor, here .
 Games played Friday, October 23 US time, Saturday, October 24 AEDT. All times AEDT. 
 Chicago Bulls 132 Milwaukee Bucks 125 (Final) 
 Josh Giddey's nine assists set up Bulls' road response at Fiserv Forum on Saturday, October 24 (AEDT) 
 Chicago Bulls guard Josh Giddey , 24, had six points, a game-high nine assists and four rebounds in 25 minutes as the Bulls answered a 43-point opening-night loss with a 132-125 win against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum on Saturday, October 24 (AEDT). He shot 3-from-9 (0-from-2 from three), with one turnover, and finished minus-15.
 He was listed as probable with a left wrist sprain on the NBA's morning injury report and cleared by the evening update , having told reporters after the opener in Toronto that he hurt the wrist in the pre-season.
 His last assist set up Leonard Miller's layup for a 117-111 lead. He checked out for good with 3:56 left and Chicago behind 119-118, and Tre Jones closed in his place as the Bulls finished on a 14-6 run.
 Milwaukee led by 15 in the first quarter before a 44-point second quarter cut it to 62-61 at half-time. Norman Powell scored 25 for Chicago, Caleb Wilson 21 and Miller 19 off the bench. Tyler Herro scored 34 for the 0-2 Bucks.
 Next: Washington Wizards at Chicago Bulls, Sunday, October 25, 11:00am AEDT.
